summary: A two-bay timber-framed cottage with a tiled gable roof, inset windows and a chimney socket, parameterised by width, depth, storeys, roof pitch and seed.
objective: Seen from about seven metres the cottage reads as three tiers of detail: gable-and-chimney silhouette, frame timbers and window recesses, then sill drips and peg heads.
example_prompts: Add four varied cottages along the village lane.
I need a half-timbered house I can reuse with different widths.
not_for: Any claim about historical joinery of a specific region or period.

silhouette: gable roof with 42 deg pitch and 25 cm eave overhang, ridge at 3.93 m above the ground plane
brick chimney breaking the ridge line and topped with a stone cap at 4.73 m
door step and threshold standing 16 cm outside the front wall plane
medium: four exposed frame timbers per long wall, 16 cm wide and standing 7 cm proud of the plaster
windows inset 12 cm behind the wall face with a 6 cm frame, cut as real holes through a 22 cm wall
roof tiles laid as overlapping strips, three rows visible per metre of slope
fine: 3 cm bevel on every timber edge, cut as geometry rather than shaded on
sill drip groove under each window, a 2.5 cm shadow line below the sill lip
peg heads at the frame joints, 7 cm across, two per timber
per-instance hue jitter of 4 percent on the tile strips

principles: Model the silhouette first: a cottage is recognised by roof pitch, chimney and eave line before any surface detail exists.
Wall thickness is what makes a building read as built. An opening cut flush with the wall plane looks like a decal at every distance.
Variation belongs in the parameters, not in the mesh: four cottages from one blueprint with four seeds beat four hand-modelled boxes.
implementation: Call create({ width, depth, storeys, seed, roofPitchDeg }); the returned group is centred on its footprint with y = 0 at the ground plane.
Attach a chimney pot, sign or lean-to through the named sockets rather than by hand-placing world coordinates.
Use the returned colliders for physics; they are axis-aligned box descriptors, not the render meshes.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.
Two instances with different seeds differ visibly in tile hue and timber placement while keeping the same silhouette.
The door socket lands on the wall face, not inside it: its z equals half the depth parameter.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here is a measurement of any real building, joinery method or material.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters, not a guarantee at every parameter combination; two storeys costs 4980 triangles and a 55 degree pitch 3580.
Tuned against ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 with no post-processing; a different exposure changes how the fine band reads.
Openings are positioned as fractions of the width, so a cottage narrower than 3 m puts its door and windows uncomfortably close together.

T2 is the same geometry with runtime procedural surface and vertex occlusion (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults); it adds no polygons and ships no files, and it reads at stylized-game quality, not photoreal.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Swap the palette and the roof material to move the cottage between the listed looks or to an unlisted one.

defaults.rationale: Proportions tuned so a 1.7 m figure reads as door-height at the door socket and the roof still dominates the silhouette at the far proof distance of twenty-seven metres.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds; footprint and ridge height only.

T2.note: Unmapped colours stay flat on purpose: pane #2f3a3f (glass) and opening shadow #3b362f.

T3.note: Blender hero tier planned in phase 9C; nothing is shipped yet.

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
